options.title: What if the Suez Canal closed for a year?
options.first_line: What if the Suez Canal, one thin ditch in Egypt, closed for a whole year?
options.first_frame: An old map of Egypt between two seas, the canal a thin blue line being drawn through the desert, a cargo ship already sailing into it.

options.title: One ditch in Egypt holds up the world
options.first_line: One ditch in Egypt carries an eighth of the world's trade. What if it closed?
options.first_frame: A long line of cargo ships queuing at the canal's mouth on an old map, a barrier swinging shut across the water.

options.title: Close the Suez Canal for a year. Then what?
options.first_line: Close the Suez Canal for one year, and every ship from Asia turns around Africa.
options.first_frame: A ship's route bending away from the canal and curling all the way round Africa on the map.

why: It names a place you can picture and asks what happens without giving any answer, whereas C's first line gives away the twist (ships go around Africa) and B's title is a flat claim that spends its big figure up front.
